Understood—I’ll keep **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor’s Degree  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Campus:** Burnaby  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **School:** School of Construction and the Environment  
- **Length:** Four years of full-time academic study  
- **Status:** Active  

The first two years provide a broad practical foundation in civil engineering. Successful completion of those first two years leads to a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** within the degree pathway. Students who meet the continuation requirements may proceed to the final two years, which include advanced engineering theory, design, project work, and a team-based capstone project.

### Related courses
The program’s course list covers Levels 1–8. Examples include:

- **CIVL 1012 — Introduction to Civil Engineering**
- **MATH 1422 — Differential Calculus for Civil Engineering**
- **PHYS 1192 — Physics for Civil Engineering 1**
- **SURV 1130 — Surveying for Civil Engineering 1**
- **CIVL 2020 — Mechanics of Materials 1**
- **CIVL 3041 — Soil Mechanics**
- **CIVL 3074 — Structural Engineering 1**
- **CIVL 4033 — Construction Management 2**
- **CIVL 4090 — Industry Project**
- **CIVL 7012 — Computational Methods**
- **CIVL 7092 — Civil Engineering Design**
- **CIVL 7089 — Capstone Design Proposal**
- **CIVL 7090 — Capstone Design Project**

The full program course list includes core courses, technical electives, Liberal Studies electives, and optional co-op work terms.

program.program_overview: The BEng in Civil Engineering is composed of four years of full-time academic study. The first two years of the degree program present a broad, practical overview of the field of civil engineering, with engineering fundamentals stressed and reinforced across the curriculum. You will receive an abundance of learning opportunities to apply these fundamentals to the solution of real-world design scenarios that would be encountered by both technologists and engineers. Throughout the program, we will present opportunities to strengthen your graphical, written, and oral communication skills. You will spend a significant amount of time on hands-on training in material testing, surveying, manual and computer-aided drafting, and receive instruction in the use of engineering software tools. You will receive a Diploma in Civil Engineering credential upon successful completion of the first two years of academic study within this degree program.  If you meet the continuation requirements, you may continue into the final two years of the degree program which are academically rigorous. We will thoroughly investigate the theoretical foundations of civil engineering science and design topics. At the same time, you will apply the practical civil engineering knowledge you have gained in course assignments and project work. You will also be challenged to view the engineer’s role from an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary perspective. You will learn about the role of the engineer in project and construction management and enrich your educational experience with complementary studies courses relating to social sciences and the humanities. To further develop your engineering skills for professional practice, you will work with classmates to complete a team-based capstone design project.

For an admissions scenario, inspect the resolved program's structured ADMISSION and INTERNATIONAL rules. Category questions must search programs by credential. content.text:
Understood—I’ll keep **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor’s Degree  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Campus:** Burnaby  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **School:** School of Construction and the Environment  
- **Length:** Four years of full-time academic study  
- **Status:** Active  

The first two years provide a broad practical foundation in civil engineering. Successful completion of those first two years leads to a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** within the degree pathway. Students who meet the continuation requirements may proceed to the final two years, which include advanced engineering theory, design, project work, and a team-based capstone project.

### Related courses
The program’s course list covers Levels 1–8. Examples include:

- **CIVL1012 — Introduction to Civil Engineering**
- **MATH1422 — Differential Calculus for Civil Engineering**
- **PHYS1192 — Physics for Civil Engineering 1**
- **SURV1130 — Surveying for Civil Engineering 1**
- **CIVL2020 — Mechanics of Materials 1**
- **CIVL3041 — Soil Mechanics**
- **CIVL3074 — Structural Engineering 1**
- **CIVL4033 — Construction Management 2**
- **CIVL4090 — Industry Project**
- **CIVL7012 — Computational Methods**
- **CIVL7092 — Civil Engineering Design**
- **CIVL7089 — Capstone Design Proposal**
- **CIVL7090 — Capstone Design Project**

The full program course list includes core courses, technical electives, Liberal Studies electives, and optional co-op work terms.

Program details: https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/

events.raw_answer:
Understood—I’ll keep **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor’s Degree  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Campus:** Burnaby  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **School:** School of Construction and the Environment  
- **Length:** Four years of full-time academic study  
- **Status:** Active  

The first two years provide a broad practical foundation in civil engineering. Successful completion of those first two years leads to a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** within the degree pathway. Students who meet the continuation requirements may proceed to the final two years, which include advanced engineering theory, design, project work, and a team-based capstone project.

### Related courses
The program’s course list covers Levels 1–8. Examples include:

- **CIVL1012 — Introduction to Civil Engineering**
- **MATH1422 — Differential Calculus for Civil Engineering**
- **PHYS1192 — Physics for Civil Engineering 1**
- **SURV1130 — Surveying for Civil Engineering 1**
- **CIVL2020 — Mechanics of Materials 1**
- **CIVL3041 — Soil Mechanics**
- **CIVL3074 — Structural Engineering 1**
- **CIVL4033 — Construction Management 2**
- **CIVL4090 — Industry Project**
- **CIVL7012 — Computational Methods**
- **CIVL7092 — Civil Engineering Design**
- **CIVL7089 — Capstone Design Proposal**
- **CIVL7090 — Capstone Design Project**

The full program course list includes core courses, technical electives, Liberal Studies electives, and optional co-op work terms.

Program details: https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/
